evidence.requirements: Every brief item is present. The start page lists title, date/time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (Tastings.jsx:26-33, start.jpg). Each card has a 'Book <title>' link (Tastings.jsx:35-37). The form has the labels Name/Email/Guests and a 'Book' button (Booking.jsx:109-114). Server rules: guests 1-8 (app.js:13-16), seat limit enforced (store.js:31-35), and field errors render under the field they concern (Booking.jsx:80-84, form.jpg). The confirmation shows the heading 'Booking confirmed', the tasting, guests, total and reference (Booking.jsx:34-46, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a 'Password' field and a 'Sign in' button, with the password from STAFF_PASSWORD (Staff.jsx:52-62, index.js:4). Bookings are grouped by tasting with a Cancel button that frees seats (Staff.jsx:97-131, store.js:43-48, staff.jpg). The interface is React with Express, zod and react-router, data is in memory, and npm start uses PORT (index.js:12). Fully booked tastings get a badge and a muted card (Tastings.jsx:24,32). Mobile CSS is in styles.css:99-111. Nothing is unmet.
evidence.correctness: The seat check and the write happen in one synchronous step (store.js:28-39), and a 10-way concurrent test confirms no overbooking (app.test.js:87-92). Zod rejects booleans, arrays, floats, blank strings and empty names (app.js:9-17), and every rejection is tested (app.test.js:40-60). The over-limit message gives the exact seats left or 'fully booked' (store.js:33). Cancelling deletes the booking so its seats come back (tested at app.test.js:154-157). The page re-fetches seats after a refusal (Booking.jsx:67-69). Unknown tastings return 404, malformed JSON returns 400 (app.test.js:94-99), and the weekday is computed in UTC so it is not shifted by timezone (api.js:14). The one weak spot is that a fully booked tasting still shows an active form and the server refuses the booking only on submit (Booking.jsx:102-115). That is handled correctly, not a bug.
evidence.security: The password check hashes both values with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual, and it refuses every password when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (app.js:40). The session is regenerated on sign-in (app.js:72). The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and secure:'auto' (app.js:36). The 8-hour session expiry is enforced on the server from the sign-in time (app.js:42-45, tested at app.test.js:174-182). Sign-in is rate-limited to 5 failures per 15 minutes (app.js:46-53). Helmet is on, the JSON body limit is 10kb, the session secret is random and not hard-coded, and the error handler hides internals (app.js:96-100). React escapes all output, and the public API does not leak booking data (app.test.js:160-164). No secrets are in the repository.
evidence.code_quality: The code is small and cleanly split: store.js holds data, app.js holds HTTP, index.js boots the server, and there is one React page per route. Validation is declarative in zod, naming is clear, and network and server errors are handled on every fetch. Two blemishes: some lines are over 150 characters (app.js:40, app.js:88, Booking.jsx:79), and Booking.jsx:67-69 has an awkward dangling indent for the re-fetch after a refusal. The Booking component mixes loading, not-found, confirmation and form states in one function. That is acceptable at this size.
evidence.tests: There are about 30 supertest/vitest API tests (server/app.test.js). They cover the listing, totals, unique references, every invalid-input case, the seat limit and fully booked state, concurrency, 404s and malformed JSON, auth rejection, cookie flags, cancelling and freeing seats, sign-out, server-side expiry and rate limiting. There are no frontend or end-to-end tests, so the brief's UI wording is not covered by regression tests: the 'Book <title>' links, the labels, the 'Booking confirmed' heading and errors shown next to their field. vite.config.js:7 only includes server tests.
evidence.ux_design: The look is coherent and fits a winery: a wine-red header with a gold rule, serif headings, cream paper cards (start.jpg). The error state is clear, with a red field border, a pink fill and a message under the field (form.jpg). The success state is a distinct green panel with a well-structured summary (confirmation.jpg). Weak points: dates are shown in ISO form '2026-11-06 18:00' rather than a guest-friendly 'Fri 6 Nov, 18:00'. The site has no imagery or description of what each tasting includes. The confirmation gives no next step (address, email, what to bring).
evidence.accessibility: Good basics: every input has a <label htmlFor>, and invalid inputs get aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing to their error (Booking.jsx:78-79, Staff.jsx:52-53). The page sets lang=en (index.html:2), and the focus-visible outline is gold (styles.css:36). The staff table has an sr-only Actions header (Staff.jsx:114) and semantic time, dl and table elements. Text contrast looks adequate (muted #655a5e and gold-text #86601f on cream). Gaps: field errors have no live region and focus is not moved to the first invalid field after submit, so screen-reader users get no announcement (Booking.jsx:80-84). Focus is not managed on route changes or when the confirmation appears. The fully booked notice lacks role=status (Booking.jsx:102). Every staff 'Cancel' button has the same accessible name, with no booking context (Staff.jsx:126).
evidence.simplicity: There are 8 runtime dependencies, each with a clear purpose (express, express-session, express-rate-limit, helmet, zod, react, react-dom, react-router-dom), and Vite with a React plugin for the build. The app is about 600 lines of source in total, with plain CSS. Nothing is over-engineered, and the forms are small enough that a form library would add little.
evidence.maintainability: The README covers install, build and start, the environment variables (STAFF_PASSWORD, PORT, TRUST_PROXY), the test and dev commands, and in-memory storage. There is one ADR on in-memory bookings plus a GLOSSARY, a package-lock.json, engines node>=22, and API regression tests. Missing: there is no CI pipeline, no .nvmrc or exact Node pin (only >=22), and no changelog or release/versioning approach beyond version 1.0.0. There is no short staff guide (sign in, cancel, the fact that a restart loses all bookings). UI behaviour has no regression tests.
evidence.visual_design: Typography is consistent (Georgia serif headings, system sans body), and the wine, gold and cream palette is coherent. Spacing and card alignment are even across start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg and staff.jpg, and the button styles are consistent (primary filled, quiet outlined, danger red outline). It looks finished but plain: a text-only header, no imagery or texture, and a bare footer. Prices as 'EUR 25' read technical rather than '€25'.
evidence.layout: The hierarchy is clear: page title, lead text, then a three-column card grid that becomes one column on phones via auto-fit (styles.css:50). On the form page the tasting summary and seats left sit above the form (form.jpg). Staff bookings are grouped into one panel per tasting with an aligned table, and on phones the table turns into labelled stacked rows (styles.css:106-110). There is no overlap or clipping in any screenshot. The start page leaves a lot of empty space below the cards at desktop width (start.jpg), and the form inputs stretch the full 62rem width, which is wider than necessary (form.jpg).
evidence.usability: Booking takes one click to the form, three fields and Book, and the confirmation shows the reference. The error messages are specific ('Only 2 seats left for this tasting.', store.js:33). Staff sign-in is direct, and there is a Staff link in the footer. Problems: Cancel acts immediately with no confirmation step and no feedback on success (Staff.jsx:71-81), so one misclick silently removes a guest's booking. Fully booked tastings still lead to a form with live fields. The guests field does not cap its max at the number of seats left before submit (Booking.jsx:111).
evidence.reception: Guests would find it trustworthy and on-brand for a small family winery (start.jpg, confirmation.jpg), and the booking reference makes it feel professional. The ISO dates, lack of tasting descriptions and absence of a confirmation email or visit details make it feel more like a functional booking widget than the winery's own site. Staff would find the grouped list clear (staff.jpg) but risky because Cancel has no undo.

strengths: Server logic is correct and well defended: seat checks are atomic, zod validation is strict and returns errors per field, and cancelling frees seats. All of it is backed by about 30 meaningful API tests, including a concurrency test.

Staff authentication is strong: SHA-256 plus timingSafeEqual comparison, session regeneration, HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookies, an 8-hour expiry enforced on the server, sign-in rate limiting and helmet.
A coherent winery look with clear error, success and fully booked states, a mobile table layout, and a very lean dependency set and codebase.
issues: Staff 'Cancel' removes a booking immediately with no confirmation, no undo and no success feedback, and every Cancel button has the same accessible name (Staff.jsx:71-81, 126).

Accessibility gaps in the booking flow: field errors are not announced (no live region), focus is not moved to the first invalid field or to the confirmation, and focus is not managed on route changes (Booking.jsx:80-84, 31-52).

Maintainability and test gaps: no CI pipeline, no exact Node pin, no release approach and no staff guide, and no UI or end-to-end tests for the brief's required labels, button texts and confirmation heading.
review.verdict: This is a solid, secure and correct booking app that meets every requirement in the brief, with a coherent winery look and thorough API tests. Before handing it to the winery, I would add a confirmation step for Cancel, announce form errors and manage focus, show guest-friendly dates, and add CI and UI tests.
